Chief_Complaint.content: Sore, cracked, dry skin on hands and fingers
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Sore, cracked, dry skin on hands/fingers

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Hand skin symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago
Symptoms are mainly located on the palms
Hand skin condition is worsening and now painful
Hand pain and skin condition are limiting ability to work
Patient has missed work for 3 days due to hand symptoms
Patient reports intermittent pruritus of the hands
Bleeding from hands occurs only after scratching
No spontaneous bleeding from the hands
Possible trigger is exposure to housekeeping and cleaning products
Symptoms are not consistent with glove use
Patient changed jobs about 4 months ago to hotel housekeeping work involving bedrooms, bathrooms, and corridors
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: changed jobs ~4 months ago (hotel housekeeping: bedrooms/bathrooms/corridors)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient tried E45 cream without benefit
Patient tried an antihistamine without benefit
Patient reports no fever or temperature elevation
Patient reports no nausea or vomiting
Patient reports no bowel issues
Patient reports no urinary symptoms
Patient reports eating, drinking, and appetite are okay
Patient otherwise feels well
Patient has mild dryness on legs that is not severe
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Other dryness: mild on legs, not severe

Family_History.content: No known family history of skin problems
No family history of bowel problems
Family_History.source_text: No FHx asthma or bowel problems

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a hotel housekeeper
Patient has inconsistent glove use at work
Patient drinks a couple of pints of alcohol per week

Assessment.content: Hand dermatitis, likely contact dermatitis related to cleaning product exposure and not wearing gloves
Assessment.source_text: Hand dermatitis, likely contact dermatitis (cleaning product exposure; not wearing gloves)

Assessment.content: Hand dermatitis characterized by pruritic, cracked, painful palms for 3–4 months, worsening and impairing work
Assessment.source_text: pruritic, cracked painful palms x3–4 months, worsening, impaired work.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise patient to avoid triggers and wear gloves at all times when cleaning
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Avoid triggers; wear gloves when cleaning at all times

Plan_of_Care.content: Start topical steroid cream for hand dermatitis
Start a stronger emollient and apply liberally 3–4 times per day for the next couple of weeks
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start stronger emollient; apply liberally 3–4x/day x next couple weeks

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescription to be sent to pharmacy
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Rx to be sent to pharmacy

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow up if not improving in 1–2 weeks (10–14 days) or sooner if worsening or spreading
Follow_up_Information.source_text: F/u if not improving in 1–2 weeks (10–14 days) or sooner if worsening/spreading

Physical_Findings.content: No physical examination or vital signs documented

Review_of_Systems.content: No fever or temperature elevation reported
Eating, drinking, and appetite are okay
